briefing.opening: Hello everyone. I will now begin the daily climate change briefing for September 24, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Warnings
sections.content: Today's major domestic and international news highlights the intensifying direct threats posed by climate change. In Busan, a shark named 'Bukang-i' appeared in an artificial waterway, signaling a warning about climate change [1, 23], and significant changes are being detected in marine ecosystems, such as the disappearance of squid in the waters of Ulleungdo and Dokdo [2]. Domestically, an analysis revealed that the average temperature during Chuseok over the past 50 years has risen by 2.2 degrees Celsius compared to the preceding 25 years, suggesting that 'cool Chuseok' is now a thing of the past [21]. Internationally, in Spain, heavy rainfall and heatwaves combined to fuel the worst wildfires [4], and in Colorado, concerns have been raised that this year's record-breaking heat could become the new normal [41]. Furthermore, the melting of glaciers in Alaska clearly shows the scars of climate change [42], and the UK released a report stating that the climate crisis poses a serious threat to national security, warning of its connection to the El Niño phenomenon [61].

sections.title: ⚠️ Policy Challenges and International Warnings
sections.content: Policy challenges for addressing the climate crisis and international warnings are also noteworthy. At the UN General Assembly, former U.S. President Donald Trump claimed the climate crisis was a 'hoax,' drawing criticism from world leaders [22], and in Canada, two new reports highlighted policy challenges by indicating that significantly more effort is needed to combat climate change [34, 51]. Alongside analyses suggesting that climate change is making daily life more expensive [48], specific economic and environmental threats are being reported, including an increase in coastal flood days [30, 38] and heightened landslide risks in the Southern Appalachians [32]. Arguments have been made that systemic changes are necessary to resolve the climate crisis [54], and a 'Warning of Atrocities' report addressing artificial intelligence and climate change was also released, urging awareness of new dimensions of threat [33].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Adaptation Efforts and Resilience Building
sections.content: Amidst the threats of climate change, efforts to strengthen adaptation and resilience are continuing both domestically and internationally. Domestically, efforts are underway to strengthen the production base of Iksan ginger, making it resilient to heatwaves and droughts [5], and in orchards, the deployment of sunshade nets has achieved tangible results, reducing heatwave damage by 34% [6]. Internationally, New York MTA has embarked on an $800 million project to protect the Metro-North Hudson Line from climate change [50], and in Belize, positive impact stories from climate adaptation and protected area initiatives have been reported [56]. The UK is set to participate in 'OceanEye,' a major new EU-led marine science program aimed at improving extreme weather event prediction, thereby striving to enhance climate resilience through international cooperation [63].

sections.title: 🌍 Accelerating Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Global efforts to achieve carbon neutrality and accelerate the transition to renewable energy are also active. Domestically, various local governments are expanding citizen participation platforms, such as encouraging participation in the Carbon Neutrality Point System [7, 10], expanding Net-Zero Energy Cafes [9], and promoting reed wetland purification and carbon neutrality practices in commercial districts [8], thereby encouraging carbon neutrality efforts. Yangju City's children's carbon neutrality drawing contest [11] and the Korea Forest Cooperative Federation's youth carbon neutrality experience program, supported by domestic timber [12], are contributing to raising awareness among future generations. In the renewable energy sector, the Incheon Haebaram Cooperative is nearing completion of its third solar power plant, established with citizen participation [18], and policy discussions are also active, with a Gurye County council member hosting a policy debate on public development and profit-sharing for renewable energy [19]. Internationally, India's Kerala state announced its goal to achieve 100% renewable energy by 2040 and reach carbon neutrality [59], and Germany is leading the transition in Europe by becoming the first to pledge a phased exit from fossil fuels by 2045 [62]. Former U.S. Vice President Al Gore marked the 20th anniversary of his documentary 'An Inconvenient Truth' by expressing his belief in winning the climate fight and emphasizing sustained efforts [65].

sections.title: 📰 Broad Discussions and Awareness of Climate Change
sections.content: Research, conferences, and public discourse on climate change are also actively unfolding. In Minnesota, scientific research is underway to investigate the effects of climate change on trees [26, 37], and new research on the climate change resilience of Western rivers is also providing clues [35]. In Salem, a climate change conference was held, conveying messages of hope and caution [31], and candid discussions about climate change are also expected at the FCAT meeting [55]. A survey on climate change, AI, and sustainable software was conducted among software developers [28], and questions about the interaction between the El Niño phenomenon and climate change have also been raised [40], indicating that awareness of climate change is spreading across various fields. The City of Bellevue is encouraging climate action ideas from young people, fostering the participation of future generations [47], and discussions are actively taking place regarding the connection between water, climate change, knowledge, and inspiring the next generation [58].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, alongside the diverse efforts and discussions underway to overcome it. Sustained attention and participation in addressing the climate crisis are more crucial than ever. This concludes the climate briefing for September 24, 2026.
